findings.obs_text: In Psa 139:23 the psalmist asks God to try him and know his thoughts: the thoughts are what the trying lays open.
findings.grounds: Try me and know my thoughts

findings.obs_text: In Lam 1:9 Jerusalem took no thought of her future and now cries out in affliction: the affliction follows the lack of thought. In Phili 1:17 some think to afflict Paul in prison: the thought aims at affliction. In 1Cor 7:26 Paul judges in view of the present distress, and in Job 15:35 trouble is conceived.
findings.grounds: thinking to afflict me in my imprisonment

findings.obs_text: In 1Sa 27:12 Achish trusted David, thinking David had made himself hated by Israel: the trust rests on a mistaken thought. In 2Ki 18:20 and Isa 36:5 the Rabshakeh asks in whom they trust and whether they think words are strength for war. In Isa 59:4 they rely on empty pleas while they conceive mischief, and in Mic 2:8 the passers-by go trustingly.

older.finding: 2Ch 32:11 | "Is not Hezekiah misleading you …?" with "On what are you trusting?" (32:10) and "Do you not know what I and my fathers have done?" (32:13). Trust is attacked through doubt of the leader and a record of power. The parallels (2Ki 18:20–22; Isa 36:5–7) are uncited | 10.9 (trust attacked); 10.5 (words that undermine)
older.reason: it states how trust works in a person; the trust collection owns it

findings.obs_text: In Psa 119:59 the psalmist thinks on his ways and turns his feet to the testimonies: the thinking leads the turning. In Jer 3:19 the Lord thought Israel would not turn from following him.
findings.grounds: When I think on my ways, I turn my feet

findings.obs_text: In Rom 14:14 no food is defiling by itself, yet it defiles the one who reckons it so: the thought makes the thing unclean for him. In 1Sa 20:26 Saul thinks David is absent because he is not clean: a mistaken thought. In Lam 1:9 Jerusalem's uncleanness is in her skirts and she took no thought of her end. In Num 5:28 and Judg 13:7 clean and unclean go with conceive in its bodily sense.
findings.grounds: it is unclean for anyone who thinks it unclean

findings.obs_text: In Pro 21:29 the upright gives thought to his ways, set against the wicked who puts on a bold face: the upright is marked by considering his way.
findings.grounds: the upright gives thought to his ways

findings.obs_text: In Judg 15:2 the father thought Samson utterly hated her, and in 1Sa 27:12 Achish thought David an utter stench to Israel: utter marks how fully the mistaken thought judges.
findings.grounds: He has made himself an utter stench to his people
